title: Combining futures
description:
Write `final class Futures` with:

- `static CompletableFuture<Integer> sumAll(List<CompletableFuture<Integer>> parts)`: completes with the sum of all the parts once they have **all** finished (an empty list gives 0 at once). If any part fails, the result fails too. It must not block: it returns straight away, even while parts are unfinished.
- `static <T> T valueNow(CompletableFuture<T> future, T fallback)`: without waiting, returns the value if the future has already completed normally, and `fallback` if it is not finished yet or failed.

The tests complete the futures by hand (`future.complete(3)`), so nothing needs a thread.
hints: `CompletableFuture.allOf(...)` completes when every part has; in its `thenApply`, each `join()` returns at once because the part is already done (lesson 8.02).
`isDone()` is also true for a failed future, so check `isCompletedExceptionally()` too before calling `join()`.
